title: Applied ML Eval Harness + Prompt Sets + Quantization + Regression Triage Playbook
author: Maya Fernandez
body:
Summary:
This playbook documents Redwood Inference's integrated process for evaluation (eval) harness usage, prompt set and benchmark management, model onboarding, quality guardrails, quantization profile integration, and regression triage. It is intended for applied ML engineers, model owners, SREs responsible for inference quality, and SEs supporting customer rollouts.

Goals:
- Provide a repeatable onboarding checklist for new models entering serving.
- Standardize prompt sets and benchmark definitions for consistent quality monitoring.
- Define quantization profile adoption criteria and validation steps.
- Describe the eval harness workflow for continuous regression detection.
- Establish a triage playbook with roles, SLAs, and escalation paths.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to all open models and internal Redwood model variants used in hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Focuses on production-serving quality for generation, chat, and reranking endpoints.
- Does not replace security/compliance approvals for restricted customers (see security-and-compliance docs).

Owners and roles:
- Model Owner: accountable for onboarding checklist, prompt sets, and final quality sign-off.
- Eval Lead: maintains the eval harness, schedules runs, and monitors regression alerts.
- Quantization Engineer: responsible for building and validating quantization profiles.
- SRE / Platform: ensures sandbox capacity for offline evals and production canaries.
- Product/PM: defines acceptance criteria and target metrics for customer-facing behavior.

High-level workflow:
1. Initial model assessment and risk classification.
2. Prompt set selection and baseline benchmarking.
3. Baseline eval harness run (functional + safety + performance).
4. Quantization profiling and validation (if applicable).
5. Canary rollout + continuous evals in prod.
6. Automated regression triage and manual review loop.

1) Eval Harness overview:
- Components: runner, dataset catalog, metric registry, CI integration, and alerting.
- Supported test types: unit prompt checks, distributional metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/EM for retrieval where applicable), embedding similarity drift, toxicity/safety scans, hallucination scoring via reference pairs, and latency/throughput profiles.
- Scheduling: nightly full-suite + per-PR smoke checks. Canary evaluation runs every 5 minutes for active canaries and hourly for broader cohorts.

Best practices:
- Keep prompt sets small for fast smoke runs and larger for nightly regression detection.
- Tag prompts with intent, difficulty, and ownership.
- Use seed control and deterministic sampling for reproducibility.

2) Prompt sets and benchmarks:
- Structure: each prompt set entry includes id, intent, input-text, expected-behavior (free-text), golden-response(s) where available, difficulty, and labels.
- Benchmarks: baseline benchmark must include at minimum: usefulness, correctness, safety, and latency percentiles (p50/p90/p99).
- Versioning: prompt sets live in Git (applied-ml/prompt-sets) and follow semantic versioning. Each change requires a PR with rationale and reviewer approval.

Example prompt set metadata table (config):
- id: email-drafting-001
- intent: email-drafting
- difficulty: medium
- expected_behavior: produce professional, concise email with provided facts
- owners: team-lead-models@example.redwood.com

3) Model onboarding checklist (minimum viable set):
- Pre-onboarding: architecture review, training dataset provenance check, license review.
- Functional: pass smoke prompts (>=95% pass rate on smoke set).
- Safety: no safety regression beyond threshold (see guardrails section).
- Performance: baseline latency within target (example: p95 < 600ms for small models, p95 < 1200ms for larger families).
- Cost: estimated per-1M-token cost and expected request mixing.
- Observability: metrics emitted (token_count, gen_latency_ms, kv_cache_hit_rate, model_version).
- Rollout plan: canary % schedule, fallback model, rollback thresholds.

4) Quality guardrails (automated + manual):
- Automated checks: profanity/toxicity filters, PII detectors, hallucination heuristics (entity hallucination rate), and safety policy classifier. Guardrail thresholds are defined per intent and risk tier.
- Manual review: for high-risk intents (finance/legal/medical), require human-in-the-loop review of failing prompts before production rollout.
- Alerting: alerts fire for metric breach (e.g., safety_score_delta > 0.05, correctness_drop > 3%), routed to #applied-ml-alerts and the Model Owner pager.

5) Quantization profiles and integration:
- Profiles: each profile is labeled by precision (e.g., int8, q4x), expected savings (%), and known model caveats.
- Adoption criteria: profile considered for serving if: accuracy delta <= predefined threshold on benchmark (e.g., avg F1 delta <= 1.5%), latency improvement > 10%, and memory reduction sufficient for deployment.
- Validation steps:
  a. Offline: run full eval harness on quantized model and compare metrics to baseline.
  b. Stress tests: run adversarial prompt set to surfaces failure modes.
  c. Canary: small percent in production with elevated monitoring.
- Example snippet (CLI):
  redwood-qprofile create --model-id m123 --profile "q4x" --notes "initial int4x profile for latency-sensitive workloads"
  redwood-eval run --profile m123:q4x --suite nightly-full

6) Regression triage playbook (on alert):
- Trigger sources: nightly eval run, canary eval, customer report, or automated CI checks.
- Immediate actions (0-30 min):
  1. Acknowledge alert in PagerDuty and post link to triage thread.
  2. Attach last successful model commit id and current model commit id to thread.
  3. If production impact: open SEV ticket and initiate rollback to last known-good model per rollout policy.
- Investigation (30 min - 4 hours):
  1. Reproduce failure locally using the failing prompt set and deterministic seeds.
  2. Check eval harness logs, metric deltas, and recent model changes (weights, tokenization, prompt templates).
  3. Compare quantization profiles and kernel selection logs if applicable.
  4. If regression is quantization-related, pin to unquantized variant and notify Quantization Engineer.
- Remediation (4 hours - 3 days):
  1. Hotfix model or prompt template if cause isolated.
  2. Run targeted eval suite and safety checks.
  3. Coordinate rollback or new canary rollout when metrics recovered.
  4. Postmortem within 3 business days if SEV triggered.

Metrics, SLOs and thresholds (examples):
- Correctness SLO: aggregated correctness score >= 0.92 across core intents (daily window).
- Safety SLO: safety violation rate <= 0.001 (alerts at 0.002).
- Latency SLO: p95 <= target per model family (tracked per route).
- Regression detection sensitivity: nightly eval should detect >0.5% metric drift with 95% confidence.

CI and automation:
- All changes to prompt sets, quantization profiles, and eval harness code must pass CI with smoke runs.
- New model PRs automatically trigger a baseline eval run; results are posted to PR and must be reviewed before merge.

Appendix — quick checklists:
- Pre-merge checklist for model PR:
  - [ ] Baseline eval run attached
  - [ ] Prompt set version updated if changed
  - [ ] Quantization regression tests (if profiles included)
  - [ ] Observability metrics added in code
  - [ ] Owner sign-off

- Canary rollback thresholds (example):
  - Correctness drop > 2% on canary prompts OR safety violation spike > 2x baseline -> immediate rollback.

Related resources:
- applied-ml-eval-harness-standards-2025
- prompt-sets-and-benchmarks-guidelines-2026
- quantization-profiles-best-practices-2026

Contact and escalation:
- Primary: Model Owner (see prompt set metadata)
- Secondary: Eval Lead (eval-lead@example.redwood.com)
- PagerDuty: #applied-ml-pager

This document will be reviewed quarterly or after any SEV impacting model quality. Changes to thresholds or core processes must be approved by the Applied ML leadership group and recorded in related_pages.
